title: Adversary Methods and Quantum Query Complexity

items.title: Finite real semidefinite programs satisfy strong duality under strict feasibility
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $n\ge1$, $m\ge0$, $A:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R^m$ be linear, $b\in\mathbb R^m$, and $C\in\mathbb S^n$, where $\mathbb S^n$ is the space of real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices with Frobenius pairing $\langle X,Y\rangle_F=\sum_{r,s}X_{rs}Y_{rs}$. Define the primal and dual values
$$p^*=\sup\{\langle C,X\rangle_F:A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\},\qquad d^*=\inf\{b^Ty:A^*y-C\succeq0\},$$
where $A^*$ is the Euclidean adjoint in these finite-dimensional coordinates. Suppose both feasible sets contain strict points, meaning $A(X_0)=b$ with $X_0\succ0$ and $A^*y_0-C\succ0$, and suppose both optimal values are finite. Then $p^*=d^*$, and both extrema are attained.

Here $X\succeq0$ means $v^TXv\ge0$ for every $v\in\mathbb R^n$, while $X\succ0$ means strict inequality for nonzero $v$.
proof_obligations: State the exact primal/dual cones, affine constraints, objective maps, and sign convention for the filtered-γ₂/adversary SDPs.
Exhibit strict feasible primal and dual points for these particular programs; prove feasibility, finite optimal values, and attainment hypotheses rather than assuming them.

Construct the exact finite-dimensional closed convex epigraph/separation set and prove it is closed; apply the existing point-versus-closed-convex separation theorem only after checking its nonempty/closed/convex hypotheses.
Derive the separating functional, identify its components with a dual feasible point and objective bound, and prove weak duality plus the reverse inequality/attainment for this SDP pair.

items.title: Effective spectral gap for a product of two reflections
items.statement_or_definition:
Let H be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, Π and Δ orthogonal projections on H, R_Π=2Π-I and R_Δ=2Δ-I, and U=R_ΠR_Δ. For 0≤ω≤π, let E_ω be the spectral projection of U onto eigenvalues e^{iφ} whose principal arguments satisfy |φ|≤ω. If Δw=0, then
$$\|E_\omega\Pi w\|\le \frac{\omega}{2}\|w\|.$$
proof_obligations: Use Jordan's lemma to decompose into invariant one- and two-dimensional blocks; compute the 2×2 rotation and bound |sin(φ/2)|≤|φ|/2.
Handle rank-zero/full blocks explicitly.

items.title: Unitary normal form for finite bit-query algorithms without extra queries
items.statement_or_definition: For any finite-input standard XOR bit-query algorithm using at most T queries on every branch, there is an algorithm with the same output probabilities whose evolution consists of an input-independent initial state, input-independent unitaries between exactly T unconditional calls to O_x, and a final measurement. It uses no controlled access to O_x and no more than T oracle calls.
proof_obligations: Apply the finite deferred-measurement dilation and retain outcome records.

For each of T query slots, route active branches through their actual address/reply registers and inactive branches through a scratch reply |+>, which is fixed by every bit-flip X; this implements branch control with one ordinary XOR call.
Pad halted/shorter branches with inactive |+> queries and verify terminal branch probabilities are unchanged.

items.title: Finite Boolean query problem and error model for adversary bounds
items.statement_or_definition:
Fix an integer N≥1, a nonempty finite set D⊆{0,1}^N, and a Boolean function f:D→{0,1}. A Boolean query problem is the tuple (N,D,f) with input x∈D and standard XOR oracle
$$O_x|i,b,w\rangle=|i,b\oplus x_i,w\rangle\quad (i\in[N],\ b\in\{0,1\}).$$
The local address register is $\mathbb C^N$ with ordered basis $|i\rangle=e_{i-1}$, $i\in[N]$. For its qubit realization, set $a=\lceil\log_2N\rceil$ and encode $i$ by the $a$-bit binary word for $i-1$. Define the total bit function $\widetilde x$ on all $a$-bit words by $\widetilde x(j)=x_{j+1}$ for $0\le j<N$ and $\widetilde x(j)=0$ for $N\le j<2^a$. The standard bit-flip query for $\widetilde x$ restricts to $O_x$ on the encoded local register and acts as the identity on unused address codewords. Algorithms in the local model use the $N$-address register at query calls.

For 0≤ε<1/2, Q_ε(f) is the least worst-case number of these oracle calls of an algorithm outputting f(x) with probability at least 1−ε for every x∈D. The input promise does not restrict the oracle address. Only query calls are counted here; no gate-efficiency assertion is part of this definition.
proof_obligations: Bind all later matrices to the finite input set D and the same query convention.
This local interface consumes the already defined query/polynomial setting without importing a physics model.

items.title: Controlled input-consistency reflection from a bit query
items.statement_or_definition:
**Inputs.** A Boolean query problem with $N\ge1$, promised input $x\in D$ accessed by its standard XOR oracle, a finite work space $K$, a one-bit control $c$, and a data register with orthogonal decomposition
$$\mathcal H=\operatorname{span}\{|start\rangle\}\oplus(\mathbb C^N\otimes K\otimes\mathbb C^2),$$
where the address basis is $|i\rangle=e_{i-1}$ for $i\in[N]$ and $|start\rangle$ is a specified unit vector orthogonal to the query summand,
and one clean scratch bit $u=0$. Fix a known address $i_0\in[N]$. Define the consistency sum
$$\Pi_x=|start\rangle\langle start|+\sum_{i=1}^N|i\rangle\langle i|\otimes I_K\otimes|x_i\rangle\langle x_i|.$$

**Output.** A gate list for the controlled plus-on-range reflection $2\Pi_x-I$ on the data register, returning the scratch bit to zero.

**Instructions.** In query mode route address $i$ to the oracle and use $u$ as its target. In start mode route the oracle address to the fixed $i_0$ and apply a Hadamard to $u$, so its query target is $|+\rangle$. Make one unconditional standard XOR oracle call. Apply phase $-1$ exactly when $c=1$, the mode is query, and the response bit $z$ differs from $u$; disable this phase on start and when $c=0$. Make a second unconditional XOR call with the same address routing. In start mode apply the Hadamard to $u$ again. Return the data and control registers and the scratch. No controlled unknown-oracle call is invoked.
proof_obligations: Specify the finite orthogonal start/query mode, response/work factors, clean scratch and comparison phase.
Give the exact two-query procedure and state that both calls are ordinary standard XOR calls, not controlled black-box access.
Defer its correctness and exact two-query property to the separate theorem items.

items.title: Input-mismatch masks and entrywise filtering
items.statement_or_definition:
For a finite Boolean query problem (N,D,f), all matrices below are indexed by the same fixed ordering of D. For i∈[N], define the input-mismatch matrix
$$(\Delta_i)_{xy}:=\mathbf 1[x_i\ne y_i].$$
For same-size matrices define the entrywise product $(A\circ B)_{xy}:=A_{xy}B_{xy}$. Define the same-output mask $F_{xy}:=\mathbf 1[f(x)=f(y)]$ and the all-ones matrix $J_{xy}:=1$. Thus $J-F$ is the opposite-output mask.
proof_obligations: Fix matrix indexing/order, real versus complex entries, and the zero-input/constant-function convention.

items.title: Query-address projectors for bit-oracle algorithms
items.statement_or_definition:
Let an N-address bit-query algorithm act on
$$\mathcal H=\mathbb C^N\otimes\mathcal H_{\rm response}\otimes\mathcal H_{\rm work},$$
where the first factor has computational basis $\{|i\rangle:i\in[N]\}$. The query-address projector is
$$\Pi_i=|i\rangle\langle i|\otimes I_{\rm response}\otimes I_{\rm work}.$$
It projects onto every state whose query address is i, regardless of response or work state.
proof_obligations: Specify address encoding and all response/work tensor factors.
Verify pairwise orthogonality and the identity resolution.

items.title: Filtered γ₂ factorization norm for query mismatch masks
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $D\subseteq\{0,1\}^N$ be a nonempty finite domain with $N\ge1$, and let $\Delta=\{\Delta_i\}_{i=1}^N$ be its input-mismatch masks from [[def-qa-16-input-mismatch-matrices]]. For any complex matrix $A$ indexed by $D\times D$, define
$$
\gamma_2(A\mid\Delta):=\inf \max\!\left\{\max_{x\in D}\sum_i\|u_{x,i}\|^2,\ \max_{y\in D}\sum_i\|v_{y,i}\|^2\right\},
$$
where the infimum is over finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and vector families satisfying
$$A_{xy}=\sum_i(\Delta_i)_{xy}\langle u_{x,i}|v_{y,i}\rangle_D\quad(x,y\in D).$$
Set the value to $+\infty$ if no such families exist. Every feasible family may be taken in dimension at most $2|D|$ for each i.
proof_obligations: State linear-first/Dirac convention, finite dimension sufficiency, attainment conditions and infeasible-support cases.

items.title: Finite, attained general adversary value for nonconstant Boolean functions
items.statement_or_definition: For a finite Boolean query problem (N,D,f), restrict to real symmetric Γ indexed by D with Γ∘F=0 and denominator d(Γ)=max_i||Γ∘Δ_i||. If f is nonconstant, every nonzero admissible Γ has d(Γ)>0, the ratio ||Γ||/d(Γ) is finite, and its supremum is a maximum. For constant f define Adv±(f)=0.
proof_obligations: Show a zero denominator forces Γ=0 because the mismatch masks cover every off-diagonal input pair and Γ has zero diagonal.
Use Frobenius/operator-norm inequalities to bound the ratio, then compactness of the normalized feasible set to prove a maximizer exists.

items.title: The controlled input-consistency circuit realizes the exact reflection
items.statement_or_definition:
Assume the distinguished vector $|start\rangle$ in the input decomposition is unit, as required by [[alg-qa-16-controlled-consistency-reflection]]. For every promised input x, that circuit realizes the control-first block operator
$$\operatorname{diag}(I_{\mathcal H},R_{\Pi_x}),\qquad R_{\Pi_x}=2\Pi_x-I,$$
where $\Pi_x$ projects onto the start vector and all query states whose response equals x_i. The controlled operation uses the plus-on-range sign, including on the distinguished start state.

The displayed consistency sum is an orthogonal projection. For arbitrary control/data superpositions, the supplied circuit restores its scratch qubit to zero, including the start mode protected by a $|+\rangle$ scratch during both unconditional calls; no controlled unknown-oracle call is required.
proof_obligations: Check the circuit on an orthonormal basis of start/query, address, reply, work, scratch and control registers.
Show the scratch bit returns to zero because the standard XOR query is self-inverse; identify the exact +1/−1 eigenspaces of 2Π_x−I.

items.title: General adversary matrix and spectral bound
items.statement_or_definition:
For a nonconstant finite Boolean query problem define
$$\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(f):= \max_{\substack{\Gamma\in\mathbb R^{D\times D},\ \Gamma=\Gamma^{\mathsf T},\ \Gamma\ne0\\ \Gamma\circ F=0}} \frac{\|\Gamma\|}{\max_{i\in[N]}\|\Gamma\circ\Delta_i\|}.$$
Negative entries are allowed. The denominator is positive and the maximum is finite and attained by [[lem-qa-16-general-adversary-finite-and-attained]]. For constant f set $\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(f)=0$. The **nonnegative adversary value** $\operatorname{Adv}(f)$ is the same maximum with the additional constraint $\Gamma_{xy}\ge0$ for all x,y; it is also set to zero for constant f.
proof_obligations: Prove the ratio is finite for nonconstant f and define the optimum/maximizer in finite dimension.
Explain signed/negative weights and distinguish this from the nonnegative Ambainis bound.

items.title: Adversary progress at initial and bounded-error final states
items.statement_or_definition:
For a standard XOR query algorithm that outputs $f(x)$ with probability at least $1-\epsilon$ for every $x\in D$, where $0\le\epsilon<1/2$, purify its final states and define
$$W_t=\sum_{x,y\in D}\Gamma_{xy}\alpha_x\alpha_y\langle\psi_x^t|\psi_y^t\rangle_D,$$
where α is a real unit eigenvector of Γ with eigenvalue of magnitude ||Γ||. Then |W_0|=||Γ|| and
$$|W_T|\le 2\sqrt{\epsilon(1-\epsilon)}\,\|\Gamma\|.$$
proof_obligations: Define W_t=Σ_{x,y}Γ_{xy}α_x*α_y⟨ψ_x^t,ψ_y^t⟩.
Prove the terminal overlap bound from opposite-output acceptance probabilities, including signed Γ and the chosen conjugation convention.

items.title: Dual vector formulation of the general adversary bound
items.statement_or_definition:
For every finite nonconstant partial Boolean function $f:D\to\{0,1\}$,
$$\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(f)=\min_{\{v_{x,i}\}}\max\{C_0,C_1\},\qquad C_b:=\max_{x:f(x)=b}\sum_i\|v_{x,i}\|^2.$$
The vectors lie in a common finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and satisfy, for all distinct $x,y$,
$$\sum_{i:x_i\ne y_i}\langle v_{x,i}|v_{y,i}\rangle_D=\mathbf1[f(x)\ne f(y)].$$
The minimum is attained. If only opposite-output constraints are initially required, tensoring each vector with $|x_i\oplus f(x)\rangle$ imposes the equal-output zero constraints without changing costs or cross-output values.
proof_obligations: Derive the SDP dual from the signed symmetric Γ program entry by entry.
Use the finite SDP duality lemma and show feasibility/attainment under the nonconstant Boolean hypotheses.
Explain balancing the 0/1 vector-family costs by reciprocal scaling.

To impose zero equal-output constraints without raising the objective, replace v_(x,i) by v_(x,i)⊗|x_i xor f(x)⟩. For terms with x_i≠y_i, the added labels coincide iff f(x)≠f(y); cross-output inner products remain unchanged and equal-output products vanish. An output-label factor alone would instead kill the required cross-output products.

items.title: Bounded-error evaluation from a dual adversary certificate
items.statement_or_definition:
**Inputs.** A finite nonconstant Boolean function $f:D\to\{0,1\}$ on $N\ge1$ input bits and a supplied finite dual-vector certificate $\{v_{x,i}\}$ in a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $V$, meaning that for every distinct $x,y\in D$,
$$\sum_{i:x_i\ne y_i}\langle v_{x,i}|v_{y,i}\rangle_D=\mathbf1[f(x)\ne f(y)].$$
Its class costs $C_b:=\max_{x:f(x)=b}\sum_i\|v_{x,i}\|^2$ satisfy $C_0,C_1\le A$ for a supplied bound $A\ge1$. The declared standard XOR input oracle is available. The input-independent controlled witness-span reflection specified below is a nonoracle operation in this query model; no efficient gate implementation for it is assumed.

**Output.** A Boolean estimate of $f(x)$ for the promised input $x\in D$.

**Instructions.** Use the finite work space
$$\mathcal H=\operatorname{span}\{|start\rangle\}\oplus(\mathbb C^N\otimes V\otimes\mathbb C^2).$$
Here the address basis is $|i\rangle=e_{i-1}$ for $i\in[N]$, and $|start\rangle$ is a specified unit vector orthogonal to the query summand.
The witness family is classical instance data used to specify a subspace, not an input-dependent state preparation. Define
$$\nu_x=1+\frac1{2A}\sum_i\|v_{x,i}\|^2,\qquad |\psi_x\rangle=\nu_x^{-1/2}\left(|start\rangle+\frac1{\sqrt{2A}}\sum_i|i\rangle|v_{x,i}\rangle|x_i\rangle\right).$$
Let $\Delta$ project onto the span of all $|\psi_y\rangle$ with $f(y)=1$, and let
$$\Pi_x=|start\rangle\langle start|+\sum_{i=1}^N|i\rangle\langle i|\otimes I_V\otimes|x_i\rangle\langle x_i|$$
project onto $|start\rangle$ plus query states whose response is $x_i$. Form the exact ordered product
$$U_x=(2\Pi_x-I)(2\Delta-I).$$

Choose $M=2^m$ as the least power of two satisfying $M\ge512A$. Initialize the data register to $|start\rangle$ and apply the coherent QPE gate list followed by its projective readout on $U_x$. Implement controlled $U_x$ in chronological order by controlled $(2\Delta-I)$, then controlled $(2\Pi_x-I)$, retaining both plus-on-range signs. Repeat that complete controlled circuit $2^j$ times for the required power $U_x^{2^j}$ at each $j=0,\ldots,m-1$. Each controlled input-dependent reflection is the two-unconditional-query consistency-reflection circuit of [[alg-qa-16-controlled-consistency-reflection]]. For the measured phase label $y$, return $1$ exactly when $y=0$ and return $0$ otherwise. No gate-complexity bound is asserted for the input-independent reflection about the full witness span or the remaining nonoracle gates.
proof_obligations: Specify all tensor registers, the orthogonal start/query mode, certificate balance and normalization ν_x.
Define the phase-estimation circuit and output threshold y=0 exactly; M is the least power of two with M≥512A.
For f(x)=1, use |ψ_x⟩ in both ranges and show |⟨start|ψ_x⟩|²=1/ν_x≥2/3.
For f(x)=0, construct |φ_x⟩=μ_x^{-1/2}(|start⟩−√(2A)Σ_i|i⟩|v_{x,i}⟩|1−x_i⟩), μ_x=1+2AΣ_i||v_{x,i}||²≤1+2A²; prove Δ|φ_x⟩=0 and Π_x|φ_x⟩=|start⟩/√μ_x.

Apply the effective spectral-gap bound with angular threshold ω=1/(4A); bound the nonzero-phase QPE probability at y=0 using the geometric-sum tail and show the combined false-positive probability is below 1/3 for M≥512A.
Do not assert an efficient gate implementation of reflection about the full witness span.
Apply the exact QC reflection sign/unitarity theorem to both R_x and R_Δ before controlling their product; preserve U_x=(2Π_x−I)(2Δ−I) exactly.

items.title: Input-distribution certificates upper-bound the nonnegative adversary value
items.statement_or_definition:
For a nonconstant finite Boolean query problem (N,D,f), let each p_x be a probability distribution on [N]. If
$$\eta:=\min_{f(x)\ne f(y)}\sum_{i:x_i\ne y_i}\sqrt{p_x(i)p_y(i)}>0,$$
then the nonnegative adversary value satisfies $\operatorname{Adv}(f)\le1/\eta$.
proof_obligations: Choose a nonnegative unit top eigenvector for an arbitrary feasible Γ.
Insert the pairwise overlap inequality into its Rayleigh quotient and bound each filtered term by ||Γ∘Δ_i|| times the squared norm of its weighted vector.

items.title: Boolean-output filtered γ₂ equals the general adversary value
items.statement_or_definition:
For every finite nonconstant partial Boolean function,
$$\gamma_2(J-F\mid\Delta)=\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(f).$$
Here F is the same-output mask, J is all ones, and Δ is the family of input-mismatch masks. The equality is exact for Boolean outputs; no larger-alphabet factor is asserted.
proof_obligations: Write primal and dual filtered-factorization SDPs and verify the finite output-code inequality.
Show the Boolean output specialization has factor exactly one.

items.title: General adversary spectral lower bound for quantum queries
items.statement_or_definition:
For every finite Boolean query problem and 0≤ε<1/2,
$$Q_\epsilon(f)\ge\left(\frac12-\sqrt{\epsilon(1-\epsilon)}\right)\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(f).$$
In particular, at ε=1/3 the coefficient is $1/2-\sqrt2/3>0$.
proof_obligations: Combine the endpoint and one-query progress estimates by telescoping.
Optimize over the attained adversary ratio and check the ε=1/3 coefficient.

items.title: The four-bit Ambainis function separates nonnegative and signed adversary bounds
items.statement_or_definition:
Let f:{0,1}^4→{0,1} equal 1 exactly on the sorted strings
$$0000,0001,0011,0111,1111,1110,1100,1000.$$
Then the nonnegative adversary value is exactly $\operatorname{Adv}(f)=5/2$, while an explicit signed-weight matrix gives
$$\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(f)>2.511486>5/2.$$
The distributions and matrices used to certify both bounds are given in the proof.
proof_obligations: List the eight one-inputs and eight zero-inputs and the full 8×8 cross matrix by Hamming-distance type.
For the nonnegative bound, verify a positive primal matrix with value 5/2 and a finite input-distribution certificate with overlap at least 2/5 on every cross-output pair.
For the signed bound, give exact rational weights, the four invariant 2×2 blocks of each filtered matrix, and a strict norm bound below 1 while the principal Rayleigh quotient exceeds 2.51.

items.title: Nonnegative and signed adversary bounds compose from below
items.statement_or_definition:
Let $f:D_f\to\{0,1\}$ be a finite partial Boolean function on $N$ bits and let $g:D_g\to\{0,1\}$ be a finite partial Boolean function on $m$ bits. Define the block domain and composed function by
$$D_h=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\in D_g^N:(g(x_1),\ldots,g(x_N))\in D_f\},\qquad h=f\circ g^N.$$
Assume $D_h\ne\varnothing$, as required for $h$ to be a Boolean query problem under [[def-qa-16-boolean-query-domain]]. Then both adversary bounds satisfy
$$\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(h)\ge\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(f)\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(g),\qquad \operatorname{Adv}(h)\ge\operatorname{Adv}(f)\operatorname{Adv}(g).$$
proof_obligations: Construct the composed adversary matrix from the outer matrix and the input-output blocks of the inner matrix, with norm-scaled identity blocks on equal-output subspaces.
Prove its norm and every filtered norm factor exactly by the finite singular-vector block decomposition.
Check that nonnegative component matrices yield a nonnegative composite matrix.

items.title: Dual reflection evaluator has bounded-error correctness
items.statement_or_definition:
For every x∈D, the dual reflection evaluator outputs f(x) with probability at least 2/3. On 1-inputs its exact common witness vector has zero phase and squared overlap with |start⟩ at least 2/3. On 0-inputs its false-positive probability is at most $3/64+1/38<1/3$.

For every supplied finite certificate with class costs at most $A\ge1$ and a unit distinguished vector $|start\rangle$ as required by [[alg-qa-16-dual-adversary-reflection-evaluator]], the witness vectors are normalized, both specified projections and their exact plus-on-range reflections are well-defined, and the stated ordered controlled product and finite QPE circuit define the evaluator. The input-independent witness-span reflection and other nonoracle gates carry no asserted efficient gate implementation.
proof_obligations: Verify ν_x≤3/2 on 1-inputs from C_1≤A.
Verify μ_x≤1+2A² and Δ|φ_x⟩=0 on 0-inputs from the dual constraints.
Use ω=1/(4A), the effective-gap norm bound, and the QPE geometric-sum bound to show false-positive probability <1/3 with M≥512A.
Track the phase-label-zero event and all normalization constants exactly.

items.title: Dual reflection evaluator query complexity
items.statement_or_definition:
For a supplied balanced dual certificate of cost A≥1, the evaluator uses exactly
$$2(M-1)\quad\text{queries},\qquad M=2^m=\text{least power of two with }M\ge512A.$$
Thus its query cost is less than $2048A$. The phase-estimation and input-independent witness-span reflections carry no asserted gate bound.
proof_obligations: The QPE schedule uses Σ_{j=0}^{m−1}2^j=M−1 controlled U_x calls.
Each controlled U_x contains one controlled input-consistency reflection costing exactly two bit queries and one input-independent span reflection costing zero queries.
Separate query count from witness preparation, span reflection, equality gates, phase-detection gates, and classical preprocessing.

items.title: General adversary bound characterizes Boolean quantum query complexity
items.statement_or_definition:
For every finite partial Boolean function f:D→{0,1}, bounded-error quantum query complexity at error at most 1/3 satisfies
$$Q_{1/3}(f)=\Theta(\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(f)).$$
For nonconstant f, the lower coefficient is $1/2-\sqrt2/3$ and the reflection evaluator gives an upper bound below $2048\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(f)$. For constant f both quantities are zero.
proof_obligations: Combine the signed-weight progress lower bound, exact Boolean filtered-γ₂/SDP duality, and reflection/phase-detection upper algorithm.
State that the 2009 span-program proof alone has a logarithmic overhead; use the later state-conversion/reflection proof for the tight upper bound.
For constant functions, both Q(f) and Adv±(f) are zero and the empty algorithm is exact; use the nonconstant dual evaluator only when Adv±(f)≥1.

items.title: Dual adversary certificate for OR_N
items.statement_or_definition:
For the partial OR problem $D=\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_N\}$, define $v_{0,i}=N^{-1/4}$ and $v_{e_j,i}=N^{1/4}\mathbf1[i=j]$. This is a balanced dual certificate with $C_0=C_1=\sqrt N$. The matrix with only the symmetric edges $(0,e_j)$ has norm $\sqrt N$ and each filtered norm 1. Hence
$$\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(\mathrm{OR}_N)=\sqrt N.$$
proof_obligations: Check every ordered cross-output and same-output vector constraint and both class costs.
Write the matching symmetric star matrix, calculate its norm and every filtered norm, and conclude equality.

items.title: A nonnegative-only adversary estimate need not capture the general bound
items.statement_or_definition:
For the partial iterates $f^{(1)}=f$ and $f^{(k+1)}=f\circ(f^{(k)},f^{(k)},f^{(k)},f^{(k)})$ of the sorted four-bit function,
$$\operatorname{Adv}^{\pm}(f^{(k)})>(2.511486)^k,\qquad \operatorname{Adv}(f^{(k)})\le(5/2)^k.$$
Thus signed adversary weights give a strict separation already at k=1 and an exponentially increasing ratio under iteration.
proof_obligations: Define the recursive domain and block composition exactly.
Use the explicit base matrices and dual distributions, the positive-adversary overlap lemma and the composition theorem to prove the two family bounds for every k≥1.
